title: Specify callsign and station-control evidence
description:
Specify identification and control evidence for the human-reviewed emission/station classification. Define candidate authorized callsign methods, identification timing during and at the end of communication, transmitting-channel treatment, overload behavior, shutdown and recovery. Account for identification airtime and control opportunities.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Documentary design only, not permission to transmit identification or select a callsign. Do not infer that identification on a convenient common channel satisfies every hopping case. No station-control implementation or external coordination occurs here.
acceptance_criteria: Independent rule-derived event tables cover identification deadlines, interrupted exchanges, restart and loss of control. EUI-64 or IPv6 is never a callsign substitute. Explicitly identify method choices still requiring human approval and provide testable inputs to narrow.08 and narrow.11.
